headline: Proxy verified on Etherscan with recognized-firm audits; implementation verification and source repo not independently confirmed this run

findings.text: OFT adapter proxy (0x6C96dE32CEa08842dcc4058c14d3aaAD7Fa41dee) on Ethereum is verified on Etherscan (abiSource: 'etherscan', verified: true per DeFiPunkd ABI API). The proxy resolves to implementation 0xCD979B10A55FCdAC23ec785CE3066c6ef8a479A4; Etherscan search results name it 'OAdapterUpgradeable' (consistent with the proxy ABI), indicating it is known to Etherscan, but independent `verified: true` confirmation of the implementation was blocked by the DeFiPunkd API permission error this run and is recorded as unknown.

No canonical GitHub source repo is pinned for USDT0 (protocol.github: none recorded). OpenZeppelin's audit announcement names 'Everdawn-Labs/usdt0-tether-contracts-hardhat' as the audited repo at commit 01cdf1d, which is the only repo reference found. No source-to-deployed-bytecode correspondence could be confirmed this run without fetching that repo.

Three audits are present in the linked audit-reports repo: (1) ChainSecurity — 'Code Assessment of the USDT0 Smart Contracts', dated 14 January 2025, covering OFT smart contracts implementing the Omnichain extension for USDT; (2) Guardian — dated 2025-01-14, covering initial core deployment and Arbitrum migration; (3) Paladin — dated 10 January 2025 (file exists in repo; PDF body not parseable this run). A fourth audit by OpenZeppelin covers the Arbitrum USDT upgrade at commit 01cdf1d (published September 2025 announcement). ChainSecurity also published a separate 'Arbitrum v2' audit (27 January 2025). All audits pre-date this assessment by ~16 months, but the protocol launched in January 2025, so these audits were performed concurrent with deployment. No follow-up audit post-January 2025 was found for the Ethereum OAdapterUpgradeable specifically.

ChainSecurity is a recognized firm (explicitly listed in the prompt checklist). Guardian Audits conducted 9 independent USDT0 audits between January and June 2025 and is broadly recognized in the Solidity ecosystem. Paladin is a less-established firm; its audit is supplementary to the two recognized-firm reports. OpenZeppelin is a recognized firm covering the Arbitrum deployment.

Audits were performed in January 2025, concurrent with the protocol's January 2025 launch. Post-audit drift cannot be assessed without a confirmed source repo. The Everdawn-Labs/usdt0-tether-contracts-hardhat repo was identified from OpenZeppelin's announcement but was not fetched this run. Drift assessment is recorded as unknown.

The proxy (0x6C96dE32CEa08842dcc4058c14d3aaAD7Fa41dee) is an EIP-1967 Transparent Proxy; implementation is 0xCD979B10A55FCdAC23ec785CE3066c6ef8a479A4. Etherscan refers to it by name 'OAdapterUpgradeable' in search results, consistent with a verified implementation. The DeFiPunkd API call for the implementation ABI returned a permission error this run, so `verified: true` for the implementation cannot be confirmed from a fetched source in this run.

steelman.red: No canonical source repo is pinned, and independent verification of the implementation contract (0xCD979B10A55FCdAC23ec785CE3066c6ef8a479A4) could not be confirmed this run; a verified proxy with an unverified implementation is effectively unverified per V6 rules.
steelman.orange: The proxy is confirmed verified on Etherscan, implementation is named by Etherscan (strongly suggestive of verification), multiple recognized-firm audits (ChainSecurity, Guardian, OpenZeppelin) cover the deployed contracts, but the implementation's verification was not independently confirmed in this run, and no source repo was fetched to establish V2 correspondence.
steelman.green: ChainSecurity (recognized firm) and Guardian audited the exact OFT contracts deployed in January 2025; the proxy is confirmed verified on Etherscan; Etherscan names the implementation contract consistently with the verified proxy ABI; a follow-up audit by OpenZeppelin covers the Arbitrum companion deployment.

rationale.verdict: Choosing orange because: the proxy is verified (V1 confirmed), ChainSecurity and Guardian are recognized firms whose audits cover the deployed contracts (V3/V4 confirmed), but (a) the implementation's verification could not be independently confirmed this run due to API permission errors (V6 scope limit rather than confirmed failure, but unresolved), and (b) no canonical source repo was fetched to establish source-to-bytecode correspondence (V2 unresolved). These two gaps prevent green under the rubric, which requires both proxy AND implementation verification and a matched public repo whose contents correspond to the explorer-visible source.

protocol_metadata.about: USDT0 is an omnichain representation of Tether's USDT built on LayerZero's OFT (Omnichain Fungible Token) standard, enabling USDT to move across chains where Tether has not deployed a native contract. On Ethereum, an OAdapterUpgradeable proxy locks USDT and emits cross-chain messages; on destination chains, OUpgradeable contracts mint or burn USDT0 tokens. Cross-chain transfers use a burn-and-mint mechanism verified by LayerZero's DVN network, with USDT collateral remaining locked on Ethereum throughout.
